items.title: Inheritance of the ABO Blood Groups

source_refs.note: Inheritance of the ABO Blood Groups: a main subheading of 18.4.1 ABO Blood Group System, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 93-94.

blocks.text: The ABO system is controlled by the gene I (“I” stands for iso-haem-agglutinogen). It is located on chromosome 9 and has multiple alleles i.e., Iᴬ, Iᴮ and i. The alleles Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant over each other. While allele i is recessive to both of them. The Iᴬ allele produces antigen-A, the Iᴮ allele produces antigen-B. Allele i does not produce any antigen. Therefore;

items: Genotypes IᴬIᴬ and Iᴬi produce antigen-A. This phenotype is called blood group A. Individual’s plasma contains anti-B antibodies.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: In ABO system, the production of anti-A and anti-B antibodies does not require any exposure to antigens. Rather, these antibodies start forming from embryonic life and continue throughout life.

items: Genotypes IᴮIᴮ and Iᴮi produce antigen-B. This phenotype is called blood group B. Individual’s plasma contains anti-A antibodies.
Genotype IᴬIᴮ produces both antigen-A and antigen-B. This phenotype is called blood group AB. Individual’s plasma does not contain anti-A or anti-B antibodies.
Genotype ii produces neither antigen-A nor antigen-B. This phenotype is called blood group O. Individual’s plasma contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies.

blocks.title: Solve the following genetic problem.
blocks.text:
• A person has blood group A while his wife has B. They have four children each with different blood group. Explain that how is it possible?
• A woman with blood group B has a child with blood group O. What are the genotypes of the mother and child? Which genotypes could the father not have?

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: In pea plants, each character that Mendel studied was controlled by a gene with two alleles. One allele was completely dominant over the other. But incomplete dominance and co-dominance do not obey this rule of dominance. Similarly, in multiple allelic system, a gene has more than two alleles, any two of which work for producing a phenotype.

blocks.alt: A table with four columns. Genotypes IAIA or IAi, IBIB or IBi, IAIB and ii. Antigens on red blood cells: a red cell with round antigen-A knobs; one with square antigen-B knobs; one with both (antigen-B and antigen-A); one with no antigens. Antibodies in plasma, drawn as Y shapes: anti-B; anti-A; no anti-A antibody and no anti-B antibody; anti-A and anti-B. Phenotypes (blood groups): A, B, AB, O.
